claim: Inactivating mutations in the MECP2 gene are the main cause of Rett syndrome (RTT).
source: Inactivating mutations in the Methyl-CpG Binding Protein 2 (MECP2) gene are the main cause of Rett syndrome (RTT).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background knowledge about RTT etiology.

claim: No treatments for RTT are currently available despite extensive research into MECP2 function.
source: Despite extensive research into MECP2 function, no treatments for RTT are currently available.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the abstract about the current state of RTT treatment.

claim: An evolutionary genomics approach using 1028 eukaryotic genomes was used to construct an unbiased MECP2 gene network.
source: Here, we used an evolutionary genomics approach to construct an unbiased MECP2 gene network, using 1028 eukaryotic genomes to prioritize proteins with strong co-evolutionary signatures with MECP2.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Three promising drug targets were identified: IRAK, KEAP1, and EPOR.
source: Focusing on proteins targeted by FDA-approved drugs led to three promising targets, two of which were previously linked to MECP2 function (IRAK, KEAP1) and one that was not (EPOR).
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: IRAK and KEAP1 were previously linked to MECP2 function.
source: Focusing on proteins targeted by FDA-approved drugs led to three promising targets, two of which were previously linked to MECP2 function (IRAK, KEAP1) and one that was not (EPOR).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as prior knowledge.

claim: EPOR was not previously linked to MECP2 function.
source: Focusing on proteins targeted by FDA-approved drugs led to three promising targets, two of which were previously linked to MECP2 function (IRAK, KEAP1) and one that was not (EPOR).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a novel finding.

claim: Pacritinib, DMF, and EPO were able to rescue different phenotypes of MECP2 inactivation in cultured human neural cell types.
source: The drugs targeting these three proteins (Pacritinib, DMF, and EPO) were able to rescue different phenotypes of MECP2 inactivation in cultured human neural cell types, and appeared to converge on Nuclear Factor Kappa B (NF-κB) signaling in inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding in the abstract.

claim: The three drugs appeared to converge on NF-κB signaling in inflammation.
source: The drugs targeting these three proteins (Pacritinib, DMF, and EPO) were able to rescue different phenotypes of MECP2 inactivation in cultured human neural cell types, and appeared to converge on Nuclear Factor Kappa B (NF-κB) signaling in inflammation.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: RTT is an X-linked dominant disorder, almost exclusively affecting females.
source: It is an X-linked dominant disorder, almost exclusively affecting females.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RTT genetics.

claim: RTT is characterized by normal early development followed by regression, loss of purposeful hand movements, and intellectual disability.
source: RTT is characterized by normal early development followed by regression, loss of purposeful hand movements, and intellectual disability (Liyanage and Rastegar, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Characteristics of RTT such as age of onset, range of symptoms, and their severity vary between patients.
source: Characteristics of the disease such as age of onset, range of symptoms, and their severity vary between patients (Neul et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The MECP2 protein has a role in transcriptional regulation but its exact mechanism of action, co-factors and downstream targets are not fully characterized.
source: The MECP2 protein has a role in transcriptional regulation but its exact mechanism of action, co-factors and downstream targets, are not fully characterized (Picard and Fagiolini, 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support about current knowledge gaps.

claim: The MECP2 protein has been linked to both gene silencing and activation.
source: The MECP2 protein, as a transcriptional regulator, has been linked to both gene silencing and activation (Horvath and Monteggia, 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: MECP2 binds methylated CG dinucleotides through its methyl-binding domain.
source: It binds methylated CG dinucleotides through its methyl-binding domain and has a transcriptional repression domain that mediates binding to co-repressor proteins (Lyst et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation support about MECP2 protein function.

claim: MECP2 has a transcriptional repression domain that mediates binding to co-repressor proteins.
source: It binds methylated CG dinucleotides through its methyl-binding domain and has a transcriptional repression domain that mediates binding to co-repressor proteins (Lyst et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The methyl-binding domain and transcriptional repression domain are hotspots for missense, nonsense, and frameshift mutations for RTT disease.
source: These two domains are hotspots for missense, nonsense, and frameshift mutations for RTT disease (Ragione et al., 2016; Krishnaraj et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Transcriptomic analyses of RTT patient postmortem brain tissues, blood samples, cell lines, and murine models have revealed hundreds of affected genes but with a low degree of overlap between studies.
source: Transcriptomic analyses of RTT patient postmortem brain tissues, blood samples, cell lines, and murine models (Shovlin and Tropea, 2018) have revealed hundreds of affected genes but with a low degree of overlap between studies (Picard and Fagiolini, 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support about transcriptomic findings.

claim: Therapies aiming to restore MECP2 loss of function are in early development stages and are not approved for patients.
source: Therapies aiming to restore MECP2 loss of function are in early development stages and are not approved for patients.
evidence: This is stated as current knowledge about therapeutic development.

claim: Current gene therapy methods show limited transduction efficiency and are unable to modify all cells in the target tissue.
source: Furthermore, current gene therapy methods show limited transduction efficiency and are unable to modify all cells in the target tissue (Gadalla et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation support about limitations of gene therapy.

claim: MECP2 overexpression is associated with severe neurological phenotypes.
source: Targeting factors downstream of MECP2 offers a promising avenue which could allow for partial amelioration of Rett symptoms, without the severe neurological phenotypes associates with MECP2 overexpression (Chao and Zoghbi, 2012; Ramocki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: BDNF is a major downstream target of MECP2.
source: One major downstream target of MECP2 is brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) (Chen et al., 2003), a key modulator of neuronal development and function.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: BDNF is a key modulator of neuronal development and function.
source: One major downstream target of MECP2 is brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) (Chen et al., 2003), a key modulator of neuronal development and function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: BDNF levels are reduced in symptomatic MECP2 KO mice.
source: BDNF levels are reduced in symptomatic MECP2 KO mice (Kline et al., 2010) and experimental interventions that increase BDNF levels improve RTT-like phenotypes (Chang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Experimental interventions that increase BDNF levels improve RTT-like phenotypes.
source: BDNF levels are reduced in symptomatic MECP2 KO mice (Kline et al., 2010) and experimental interventions that increase BDNF levels improve RTT-like phenotypes (Chang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: IGF-1 protein potentiates BDNF activity.
source: The IGF-1 protein potentiates BDNF activity, and treatments with recombinant human IGF-1 and its analogs have led to improvement in several clinical measurements (Khwaja et al., 2014; Glaze et al., 2019), with a trial of an IGF-1 synthetic analog currently in Phase 3 (NCT04181723).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Treatments with recombinant human IGF-1 and its analogs have led to improvement in several clinical measurements.
source: The IGF-1 protein potentiates BDNF activity, and treatments with recombinant human IGF-1 and its analogs have led to improvement in several clinical measurements (Khwaja et al., 2014; Glaze et al., 2019), with a trial of an IGF-1 synthetic analog currently in Phase 3 (NCT04181723).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: A trial of an IGF-1 synthetic analog is currently in Phase 3.
source: The IGF-1 protein potentiates BDNF activity, and treatments with recombinant human IGF-1 and its analogs have led to improvement in several clinical measurements (Khwaja et al., 2014; Glaze et al., 2019), with a trial of an IGF-1 synthetic analog currently in Phase 3 (NCT04181723).
evidence: This is stated as current clinical trial information.

claim: Phylogenetic profiling analyzes gene conservation patterns across an evolutionary related set of organisms.
source: A well-tested approach for gene functional prediction and identification of functional gene networks is phylogenetic profiling (PP), which analyzes gene conservation patterns across an evolutionary related set of organisms (Pellegrini et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated with citation support as a methodological description.

claim: Genes with similar evolutionary patterns are functionally coupled, irrespective of sequence homology.
source: Genes with similar evolutionary patterns are functionally coupled, irrespective of sequence homology (Date and Marcotte, 2003).
evidence: This is stated with citation support as a principle of phylogenetic profiling.

claim: PP was used successfully to predict protein function.
source: PP was used successfully to predict protein function (Enault et al., 2004; Eisen and Wu, 2002; Jiang, 2008; Merchant et al., 2007), protein interactions (Kim and Subramaniam, 2006; Sun et al., 2005) and protein localization within the cell (Marcotte et al., 2000; Pagliarini et al., 2008; Avidor-Reiss et al., 2004; Hodges et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: PP was used successfully to predict protein interactions.
source: PP was used successfully to predict protein function (Enault et al., 2004; Eisen and Wu, 2002; Jiang, 2008; Merchant et al., 2007), protein interactions (Kim and Subramaniam, 2006; Sun et al., 2005) and protein localization within the cell (Marcotte et al., 2000; Pagliarini et al., 2008; Avidor-Reiss et al., 2004; Hodges et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: PP was used successfully to predict protein localization within the cell.
source: PP was used successfully to predict protein function (Enault et al., 2004; Eisen and Wu, 2002; Jiang, 2008; Merchant et al., 2007), protein interactions (Kim and Subramaniam, 2006; Sun et al., 2005) and protein localization within the cell (Marcotte et al., 2000; Pagliarini et al., 2008; Avidor-Reiss et al., 2004; Hodges et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations.

claim: The top 200 genes most correlated with MECP2 across eukaryotes showed high correlation (R>0.47).
source: We selected the top 200 genes (the 'E200' set), which showed high correlation (R>0.47) with MECP2.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the phylogenetic profiling analysis.

claim: The top 200 genes most correlated with MECP2 within mammals showed high correlation (R>0.49).
source: Similarly, we used NPP scores within the mammalian clade (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) to select the top 200 mammal-centric genes (the 'M200' set), which also showed high MECP2 correlations (R>0.49) (Supplementary file 1) [code is available on GitHub (Unterman et al., 2021; copy archived at swh:1:rev:14063b44a40688a8024a06347b63cfdac74b96ad)].
evidence: This is stated as a result of the phylogenetic profiling analysis.

claim: E200 and M200 had 10 genes in common.
source: The E200 and M200 lists had 10 genes in common (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The 390 gene union set was enriched with genes expressed in the brain (p-value < 0.00024).
source: A GeneAnalytics query of the 390 gene union set revealed it was enriched with genes expressed in the brain (p-value < 0.00024), with 79 genes linked to the cerebral cortex and 54 to the cerebellum (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Ben-Ari Fuchs et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and reference to a figure.

claim: 79 genes from the 390 gene union set were linked to the cerebral cortex.
source: A GeneAnalytics query of the 390 gene union set revealed it was enriched with genes expressed in the brain (p-value < 0.00024), with 79 genes linked to the cerebral cortex and 54 to the cerebellum (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Ben-Ari Fuchs et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a result of GeneAnalytics query.

claim: 54 genes from the 390 gene union set were linked to the cerebellum.
source: A GeneAnalytics query of the 390 gene union set revealed it was enriched with genes expressed in the brain (p-value < 0.00024), with 79 genes linked to the cerebral cortex and 54 to the cerebellum (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Ben-Ari Fuchs et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a result of GeneAnalytics query.

claim: Only 24 of the 390 gene list were overlapping with a length-matched list of MECP2 interactions from STRING.
source: Only 24 of the 390 gene list were overlapping with a length-matched list of MECP2 interactions from STRING (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,E), highlighting the complementary role phylogenetic analysis to other measurements and predictions of protein interaction.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison result.

claim: Open Targets identified protein-compound interactions for 11 proteins from the 390 candidate gene list.
source: Open Targets identified such protein-compound interactions for 11 proteins from our list, and DGIdb identified an additional 22, resulting in 33 druggable proteins in the MECP2 phylogenetic network.
evidence: This is stated as a result of database searches.

claim: DGIdb identified protein-compound interactions for an additional 22 proteins from the 390 candidate gene list.
source: Open Targets identified such protein-compound interactions for 11 proteins from our list, and DGIdb identified an additional 22, resulting in 33 druggable proteins in the MECP2 phylogenetic network.
evidence: This is stated as a result of database searches.

claim: 33 druggable proteins were identified in the MECP2 phylogenetic network.
source: Open Targets identified such protein-compound interactions for 11 proteins from our list, and DGIdb identified an additional 22, resulting in 33 druggable proteins in the MECP2 phylogenetic network.
evidence: This is stated as a result of database searches.

claim: IRAK1 and EPOR were found in both the eukaryotic E200 and the mammalian M200 lists.
source: Two of the 33 druggable NPP-linked proteins (IRAK1 and EPOR) were found in both the eukaryotic E200 and the mammalian M200 lists, and were targeted by compounds with clinical efficacy and acceptable safety profiles (Pacritinib and EPI), making these immediately attractive for further study.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the analysis.

claim: IRAK1 was one of the six proteins functionally linked to MECP2 in a STRING functional interaction map.
source: In a STRING (Szklarczyk et al., 2019) functional interaction map, which is based on independent data types, IRAK1 was one of the six proteins functionally linked to MECP2, whereas EPOR had no known functional links (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to STRING database and Figure 2A.

claim: EPOR had no known functional links to MECP2 in a STRING functional interaction map.
source: In a STRING (Szklarczyk et al., 2019) functional interaction map, which is based on independent data types, IRAK1 was one of the six proteins functionally linked to MECP2, whereas EPOR had no known functional links (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to STRING database and Figure 2A.

claim: IRAK1 is directly adjacent to MECP2 on an evolutionary conserved chromosomal band on the X chromosome.
source: Indeed, IRAK1 is directly adjacent to MECP2 on an evolutionary conserved chromosomal band on the X chromosome (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to figures showing chromosomal location.

claim: The chr19p13.2 band contained more MECP2 co-evolved genes than any other in the genome.
source: In a chromosomal clustering analysis of all MECP2-linked genes, the chr19p13.2 band contained more MECP2 co-evolved genes than any other in the genome (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a result of chromosomal clustering analysis with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The chr19p13.2 domain contained 5 of the 33 druggable MECP2 coevolved genes: EPOR, DNMT1, ICAM1, ICAM3, and KEAP1.
source: Unexpectedly, this 5.6 Mb domain contained 5 of the 33 druggable MECP2 coevolved genes - EPOR, DNMT1, ICAM1, ICAM3, and KEAP1 (Figure 2D), making this the most strongly enriched band in the genome (p<1E-5, Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and reference to figures.

claim: The chr19p13.2 band is the most strongly enriched band in the genome for druggable MECP2 coevolved genes (p<1E-5).
source: Unexpectedly, this 5.6 Mb domain contained 5 of the 33 druggable MECP2 coevolved genes - EPOR, DNMT1, ICAM1, ICAM3, and KEAP1 (Figure 2D), making this the most strongly enriched band in the genome (p<1E-5, Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support.

claim: The entire chr19p13.2 gene cluster defines a single TAD based on high-resolution Hi-C mapping.
source: Topologically Associated Domains (TADs) define the 3D organization of functionally co-regulated gene clusters (Fritz et al., 2019), and the entire chr19p13.2 gene cluster defines a single TAD-based high-resolution Hi-C mapping (Rao et al., 2014; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and reference to Figure 2E.

claim: The chr19p13.2 region has been shown to be bound by MECP2.
source: Additionally, this region has been shown to be bound by MECP2 (Yasui et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: IRAK1 has been identified as a key intermediary in NF-κB signaling in RTT.
source: IRAK1 has been identified as a key intermediary in NF-κB signaling in RTT, with MECP2 directly binding the IRAK1 promoter to regulate its expression in MECP2-null mouse brains and NFΚB1 dramatically increasing lifespan in MECP2 null mice (Kishi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: MECP2 directly binds the IRAK1 promoter to regulate its expression in MECP2-null mouse brains.
source: IRAK1 has been identified as a key intermediary in NF-κB signaling in RTT, with MECP2 directly binding the IRAK1 promoter to regulate its expression in MECP2-null mouse brains and NFΚB1 dramatically increasing lifespan in MECP2 null mice (Kishi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: NFΚB1 dramatically increases lifespan in MECP2 null mice.
source: IRAK1 has been identified as a key intermediary in NF-κB signaling in RTT, with MECP2 directly binding the IRAK1 promoter to regulate its expression in MECP2-null mouse brains and NFΚB1 dramatically increasing lifespan in MECP2 null mice (Kishi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Pacritinib is a JAK2/FLT3 inhibitor with IRAK1 inhibiting capabilities.
source: Pacritinib is a JAK2/FLT3 inhibitor with IRAK1 inhibiting capabilities (Jensen et al., 2017), presently under clinical investigation for myelofibrosis and glioblastoma.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Pacritinib is presently under clinical investigation for myelofibrosis and glioblastoma.
source: Pacritinib is a JAK2/FLT3 inhibitor with IRAK1 inhibiting capabilities (Jensen et al., 2017), presently under clinical investigation for myelofibrosis and glioblastoma.
evidence: This is stated as current clinical information.

claim: Pacritinib is currently the only clinical stage IRAK1 inhibitor with known clinical efficacy and acceptable safety even after prolonged administration.
source: As it is currently the only clinical stage IRAK1 inhibitor with known clinical efficacy and acceptable safety even after prolonged administration (Singer et al., 2018), we chose this compound for our functional studies to target IRAK1.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: EPOR forms a heterodimer with β common receptor (βCR), also known as the Tissue-Protective Receptor (TPR).
source: EPOR forms a heterodimer with β common receptor (βCR), also known as the Tissue-Protective Receptor (TPR) (Brines et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The endogenous hormone EPO binds the TPR activating signaling cascades with roles in neuroprotection.
source: The endogenous hormone EPO binds the TPR activating signaling cascades with roles in neuroprotection (Rey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Several variants of erythropoietin lacking hematopoietic effects have been developed and shown to preserve the neuroprotective effects of EPO administration.
source: EPO has a very well understood pharmacological profile, and several variants of erythropoietin lacking hematopoietic effects have been developed and shown to preserve the neuroprotective effects of EPO administration (Chen et al., 2015; Patel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: KEAP1 is the key repressor of the transcription factor NFE2L2.
source: KEAP1 is the key repressor of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NFE2L2), which is involved in response to antioxidants through its transcriptional regulation of inflammatory pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: NFE2L2 is involved in response to antioxidants through its transcriptional regulation of inflammatory pathways.
source: KEAP1 is the key repressor of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NFE2L2), which is involved in response to antioxidants through its transcriptional regulation of inflammatory pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Dimethyl fumarate (DMF) is an approved treatment for both multiple sclerosis and psoriasis.
source: Dimethyl fumarate (DMF) is an approved treatment for both multiple sclerosis and psoriasis (Torkildsen et al., 2016; Blair, 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: DMF administration decreases KEAP1 levels, increases NFE2L2 levels and causes dissociation and nuclear transport of NFE2L2.
source: Its administration decreases KEAP1 levels, increases NFE2L2 levels and causes dissociation and nuclear transport of NFE2L2.
evidence: This is stated as a mechanism of DMF action.

claim: DMF treatment has proven to be effective and safe in conferring neuroprotection.
source: DMF treatment has proven to be effective and safe in conferring neuroprotection (Montes Diaz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: MECP2 silencing by lentivirus vectors reduced MECP2 expression by over 80% in neural cells.
source: The expression of MECP2 was silenced by over 80% in these cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to a figure showing western blot data.

claim: MECP2 silencing induced a relative increase in the expression of M1 markers (IL1, and CD86) in microglia.
source: MECP2 silencing induced a relative increase in the expression of M1 markers (IL1, and CD86) and a relative decrease of M2 markers (CD206 and IL-13) (Figure 3A), suggesting an increase in neuroinflammation.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: MECP2 silencing induced a relative decrease of M2 markers (CD206 and IL-13) in microglia.
source: MECP2 silencing induced a relative increase in the expression of M1 markers (IL1, and CD86) and a relative decrease of M2 markers (CD206 and IL-13) (Figure 3A), suggesting an increase in neuroinflammation.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: MECP2 silencing decreased the phagocytosis of microglia cells.
source: We also found that MECP2 silencing decreased the phagocytosis of the microglia cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing phagocytosis assay data.

claim: MECP2 silenced NSCs displayed preferential expression of the glial differentiation marker (GFAP) with a concomitant decrease in expression of the neuronal differentiation marker (MAP2).
source: In accordance with previous reports (Andoh-Noda et al., 2015; Mok et al., 2020), we found that MECP2 silenced NSCs displayed preferential expression of the glial differentiation marker (GFAP) with a concomitant decrease in expression of the neuronal differentiation marker (MAP2) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and reference to Figure 3C showing luciferase activity data.

claim: MECP2 silenced astrocytes expressed lower levels of EAAT2.
source: The MECP2 silenced astrocytes expressed lower levels of Excitatory Amino Acid Transporter 2 (EAAT2), indicating impaired function of these cells, as was suggested for mouse astrocytes (Okabe et al., 2012; Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and reference to Figure 3D showing western blot data.

claim: MECP2 silencing decreased the expression of BDNF mRNA in both astrocyte and neuronal cultures.
source: We finally examined the effects of MECP2 silencing on the expression of BDNF in human neurons and astrocytes and found that, as reported for mouse cells (Chang et al., 2006; Li et al., 2012), MECP2 silencing decreased the expression of BDNF mRNA in both astrocyte and neuronal cultures (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and reference to Figure 3E showing RT-PCR data.

claim: DMF, EPO, and pacritinib did not exert a toxic effect on microglia cells, astrocytes, primary neuronal cells or NSCs in the concentration ranges used.
source: We first demonstrated that in the concentrations range we used, none of these compounds exerted a toxic effect on neither microglia cells, astrocytes, primary neuronal cells nor NSCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 2 showing LDH assay data.

claim: EPO abrogated the effects of MECP2 silencing in all five marker genes (CD206, IL-13, CD86, IL-1, TNF-α) in microglia.
source: EPO exerted the most significant effect, abrogating the effects of MECP2 silencing in all five marker genes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: DMF abrogated the effects of MECP2 silencing in CD206, CD86, and IL-1, but failed to abrogate the effects on IL-13 and TNF-α in microglia.
source: In contrast, both DMF and pacritinib exerted only partial effects, abrogating the effects of MECP2 silencing in CD206, CD86, and IL-1, but failing to abrogate the effects on IL-13 and TNF-α (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figures 4B-C showing RT-PCR data.

claim: Pacritinib abrogated the effects of MECP2 silencing in CD206, CD86, and IL-1, but failed to abrogate the effects on IL-13 and TNF-α in microglia.
source: In contrast, both DMF and pacritinib exerted only partial effects, abrogating the effects of MECP2 silencing in CD206, CD86, and IL-1, but failing to abrogate the effects on IL-13 and TNF-α (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figures 4B-C showing RT-PCR data.

claim: Treatment of MECP2 silenced microglia cells with DMF exerted a significant increase in phagocytosis.
source: Treatment of MECP2 silenced cells with DMF exerted a significant increase in the phagocytosis of the silenced cells, whereas EPO and pacritinib did not (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4D showing phagocytosis assay data.

claim: EPO and pacritinib did not significantly increase phagocytosis in MECP2 silenced microglia cells.
source: Treatment of MECP2 silenced cells with DMF exerted a significant increase in the phagocytosis of the silenced cells, whereas EPO and pacritinib did not (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4D showing phagocytosis assay data.

claim: Knockdown of MECP2 leads to increased NF-κB activity in neuronal and myeloid cells.
source: Knockdown of MECP2 has been reported to lead to increased NF-κB activity in neuronal and myeloid cells (O'Driscoll et al., 2015) and this deregulated activity has been associated with neuroinflammation and decreased dendritic arborization and spine density in a mouse model of RTT (Kishi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Deregulated NF-κB activity has been associated with neuroinflammation and decreased dendritic arborization and spine density in a mouse model of RTT.
source: Knockdown of MECP2 has been reported to lead to increased NF-κB activity in neuronal and myeloid cells (O'Driscoll et al., 2015) and this deregulated activity has been associated with neuroinflammation and decreased dendritic arborization and spine density in a mouse model of RTT (Kishi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: EPO and DMF significantly downregulated the increased NF-κB activation in MECP2-silenced microglia cells.
source: A significant increase in NF-κB-dependent luciferase activation was observed for EPO and DMF in the MECP2-silenced cells (Figure 4E), indicating that EPO and DMF were able to downregulate the increased NF-κB activation in MECP2 KD cells.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4E showing luciferase assay data.

claim: Loss or impaired function of MECP2 affects the functions of glial cells and these changes have been implicated in the pathogenesis of RTT.
source: Since all three selected compounds were associated with changes in neuroinflammation, we first focused on microglia and astrocytes. Loss or impaired function of MECP2 has been reported to affect the functions of glial cells and these changes have been implicated in the pathogenesis of RTT (Kahanovitch et al., 2019; Jin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Treatment of MECP2-silenced NSCs with pacritinib or DMF did not have significant effects on markers of neuronal (βIII tubulin) or astrocytic (GFAP) differentiation.
source: Treatment of the silenced NSCs with pacritinib or DMF did not have significant effects on markers of neuronal (βIII tubulin) or astrocytic (GFAP) differentiation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: EPO abrogated the impaired NSC differentiation as reflected by an increase of βIII tubulin and a decrease of GFAP.
source: In contrast, EPO abrogated the impaired NSC differentiation as reflected by an increase of βIII tubulin and a decrease of GFAP (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: Treatment of MECP2-silenced astrocytes with EPO inhibited the decreased EAAT2 expression.
source: Treatment of these cells with EPO inhibited the decreased EAAT2 expression, whereas pacritinib and DMF did not have a significant effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5B showing RT-PCR data.

claim: Pacritinib and DMF did not have a significant effect on EAAT2 expression in MECP2-silenced astrocytes.
source: Treatment of these cells with EPO inhibited the decreased EAAT2 expression, whereas pacritinib and DMF did not have a significant effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5B showing RT-PCR data.

claim: DMF and EPO induced an increase in BDNF mRNA in MECP2-silenced neurons.
source: DMF and EPO induced an increase in BDNF mRNA in the silenced neurons (Figure 6A) and in the silenced astrocytes (Figure 6B), whereas pacritinib did not exert a significant effect in either.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A showing RT-PCR data.

claim: DMF and EPO induced an increase in BDNF mRNA in MECP2-silenced astrocytes.
source: DMF and EPO induced an increase in BDNF mRNA in the silenced neurons (Figure 6A) and in the silenced astrocytes (Figure 6B), whereas pacritinib did not exert a significant effect in either.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6B showing ELISA data.

claim: Pacritinib did not exert a significant effect on BDNF expression in MECP2-silenced neurons or astrocytes.
